rejected.name: nwnnsscomp
rejected.why: The standard NSS compiler is not one program. At least six builds circulate (TSLPatcher, KOTOR Tool, v1.3, KOTOR Scripting Tool, DeNCS, knsscomp) and they disagree on command-line syntax so completely that PyKotor identifies which one you have by SHA-256 of the executable before deciding how to call it. Its own source comments that no version offers backwards compatibility with any other. KOTOR Forge sidesteps the whole problem: PyKotor compiles NSS to NCS in-process, which is what HoloPatcher already does.

rejected.name: KOTOR Tool (Fred Tetra)
rejected.why: Still the tool every old tutorial assumes, and still the most-downloaded extractor on Deadly Stream. It has had no update since January 2013, requires .NET Framework 1.1 (long EOL, needs compatibility shims on modern Windows), is Windows-only, has no scriptable CLI, and its DLG editor is known-broken. Its ERF builder remains its most reliable component. Nothing about it belongs in an automated pipeline.

rejected.name: MDLedit
rejected.why: The binary-to-ASCII model compiler modders reach for. Version 1.0.3 shipped in November 2017 and nothing has followed; the OpenKotOR mirror of it is archived. It is GUI-only, so it cannot be driven. For models, PyKotor's mdl module handles both binary and ASCII in-process, and KotorBlender handles anything needing actual mesh work.

rejected.name: Vortex
rejected.why: Nexus Mods' manager does have an official KOTOR extension registering both games. But read its installer code: if an archive contains tslpatcher.exe or a tslpatchdata folder, it raises a hard error and refuses to install. That excludes most substantial KOTOR II mods. Vortex handles loose-override and root-structure mods only.

rejected.name: KotorMCP
rejected.why: An MCP server on PyKotor already exists on PyPI, by the same author. It is worth knowing about: five tools, a sensible installation-caching design, and LLM-shaped resource summaries. But every one of its tools is read-only, its last release was December 2025, and its declared source repository returns 404 under both of the org names it has lived at. Useful as a design precedent; not a dependency.

rejected.name: xoreos-tools
rejected.why: Actively maintained and genuinely good: unerf, unrim, gff2xml, tlk2xml, convert2da, ncsdis, ncsdecomp. But it is a set of external binaries that duplicate what PyKotor already does in-process, and it is GPL-3.0 where PyKotor is LGPL. The one thing it has that nothing else does is unobb, for Aspyr's mobile and console virtual filesystem. Kept on the shelf for exactly that.

watched.name: HolocronToolset
watched.why: The GUI editor suite over the same PyKotor library this server uses. Runs with no install via uvx holocrontoolset. The right tool when the job is visual -- editing a dialogue tree or placing objects in an area -- rather than scriptable.

watched.name: KotorBlender
watched.why: Blender addon for MDL import/export with animations and walkmeshes, plus LYT and PTH. The real model pipeline. Drivable headlessly via blender --background --python if model work ever needs automating.

watched.name: KOTORModSync
watched.why: Orchestrates multi-mod installs by driving TSLPatcher/HoloPatcher from a TOML instruction file. The closest thing the community has to a reproducible mod build, and the reason HoloPatcher grew a CLI at all.

watched.name: bioware-kaitai-formats
watched.why: BioWare's formats written as Kaitai Struct .ksy definitions, which compile to parsers in several languages. PyKotor already vendors generated output from it. The best machine-readable spec oracle available when a byte layout needs checking.

watched.name: KotOR.js
watched.why: The most active Odyssey-engine reimplementation, in TypeScript, running in a browser. Valuable as living documentation of how the engine actually interprets these formats.

watched.name: reone
watched.why: Clean-room C++ reimplementation. Notable for a real NCS decompiler built on an expression-tree IR, and for tooling that generates LIP lipsync data from audio.
